papers.title: Quantum gates with parametrically driven multi-qubit couplers
papers.abstract: Superconducting quantum processors could significantly profit from enhanced connectivity together with precise control of interactions and gates between qubits. Here we investigate plaquettes of four qubits that are coupled via a central tunable coupling circuit, so that not only gates between qubits connected by an edge of the plaquette can be executed but also between qubits across the diagonal. By numerically and analytically analyzing parametrically driven processes, we explore $\sqrt{\text{iSWAP}}$-gates between any pair of qubits, also across the diagonal, as well as three-qubit interactions and gates. For experimentally available circuit parameters, we for example find $\sqrt{\text{iSWAP}}$-gates with a gate time of 50 ns and 99.9\% fidelity, which is decreased to 99.4\% if two such gates are executed in parallel on disjoint qubit pairs in the plaquette. For three-qubit gates we find fidelities of 95\% fidelity at a gate time of 200 ns.

similar_to.title: A tunable coupling scheme for implementing high-fidelity two-qubit gates
Realization of high-fidelity CZ and ZZ-free iSWAP gates with a tunable coupler

summary.summary: This work demonstrates parametrically driven multi-qubit couplers based on dc-SQUIDs and tunable SNAILs for realizing high-fidelity gates between any pair of qubits in a four-qubit plaquette, including diagonal couplings, as well as native three- and four-qubit interactions. By carefully analyzing the Jacobi-Anger expansion of the time-dependent Hamiltonian and optimizing the drive parameters, the authors achieve $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates with 99.9% fidelity in 50 ns for two qubits and 95% fidelity in 200 ns for three-qubit gates, while also demonstrating simultaneous execution of two disjoint two-qubit gates at 99.4% fidelity.
summary.motivation: Multi-qubit couplers can enhance connectivity in superconducting quantum processors and enable direct gates between non-nearest-neighbor qubits without requiring SWAP-based routing, reducing circuit depth and coupler overhead by approximately a factor of two in 2D arrays.
summary.method: The authors modeled dc-SQUID and SNAIL couplers capacitively coupled to four transmon qubits (with detunings spanning 5.5–7.1 GHz for the SQUID setup), applied the irrotational gauge to correctly handle time-dependent external flux drives, and expanded the driven Hamiltonian using Jacobi-Anger expansions to identify resonance conditions for selective interactions. Full four-qubit Hilbert space simulations with QuTiP using super-Gaussian pulse envelopes (rank $r=8$) optimized gate fidelities via parameter tuning and Z-phase corrections.
summary.result: iSWAP gates achieved 99.9% (4-qubit) and 99.98% (2-qubit subsystem) fidelity in 48–64 ns across all geometries; parallel two-qubit gates reached 99.35% fidelity; three-qubit native gates ($a_1^\dagger a_2^\dagger a_3 + \mathrm{h.c.}$) achieved 95.5% fidelity in 200 ns and require only 54 CNOT equivalents versus 93 gates for standard decomposition; four-qubit gates gave 79.3% fidelity in 46 ns but remain limited by weak coupling strength.
